report.answer: Under the UK Data Protection Act 2018, a child can consent to information society services at age 13; the UK does not apply the GDPR default age of 16. The operative provision is section 9 of the Data Protection Act 2018, which substitutes 13 years for 16 years in Article 8(1) of the GDPR.
report.why: The ICO guidance confirms that children aged 13 and over can give their own consent for information society services when consent is the lawful basis, and that parental consent is required for those under 13. The legislation.gov.uk text of section 9 of the Data Protection Act 2018 states that references to 16 years in Article 8(1) of the GDPR are to be read as 13 years.
